title: Not Over

source.program: Obama, United for Georgia rally (The New Indian Express upload)
source.title: Oil prices up, no relief for Americans soon: Obama on ongoing US-Israel war on Iran
source.note: Georgia rally (podium sign); exact date unconfirmed — same stump lines given 10-24 in Detroit and Cleveland; upload 10-28. Vertical re-cut with a news banner — kept as is (Sailor, 10-31)

object.label: The Iran war's cost at the pump, the week before the midterm (sp01's object — History restarting — at layer 1)

legislative.note: no war authorization; Collins's nine votes against (her count) are the Senate's record; gas $2.98 pre-war → $4.29 on 10-26, diesel record over $6 (AP via Fortune)

zAxis.pos: the war delivers for the audience — worth what it costs, prices come down
zAxis.neg: it doesn't — prices stay up, the war goes on

transformNote: one of three same-week voices on the war and the pump, read side by side

trace.shadowNote: relief — lower prices and the war over

positions.fluid: no nuclear weapons · not over · no relief

log.what: cut for sp01 block 3 ('This week'). Scores are Claude's proposals, unruled; Sailor's election hypothesis is sealed and played no part

scoreboard.zRule: every line carries a z, inferred where implied (Sailor 2026-10-13); inferred lines are marked zInferred with a zWhy

lines.quote: the original rationale was to get them to give up their nuclear weapons… except Iran didn't have nuclear weapons
I had put in place a deal that everybody acknowledged kept them from getting nukes. I didn't have to fire any missiles
lines.note: his own record as the comparison ('everybody acknowledged' overstates — the JCPOA had loud critics)

lines.quote: eight months later… our allies and bases attacked, Americans killed, hundreds wounded, our missiles run down
Iran now has veto power over the Strait of Hormuz
this is the reason the price of oil is up… the price of diesel… just about everything
contrary to the promises… this war is not over. It's still going on
lines.note: the promise checked against the record

lines.quote: you are not getting any relief anytime soon

lines.why: It disputes the stated rationale for the war, which is about justification rather than its costs, flows, votes, or deaths.
It is a counterfactual claim about the prior nuclear deal and what it prevented, which is a judgment about the argument rather than the war's measurable cost.
It names concrete war costs (attacks on allies and bases, Americans killed and wounded, depleted missile stocks), which are part of the object's substance.
It describes a flow constraint through the Strait of Hormuz, the mechanism that the crude price series tracks.
It attributes the rise in crude, diesel, and wider prices to the war, which matches the tracked crude and gasoline increases.
It says the war is continuing against prior promises, a status claim that bears on the z-axis outcome but is aimed at winning the room.
It forecasts that pump-price relief will not come soon, a claim about the cost the object is measured by, aimed at the audience.

lines.why: It disputes the war's stated rationale rather than any cost, flow, vote, or death, so it argues about the justification instead of the price at the pump.
It sets the war against a deal that worked without missiles, pressing the cost-benefit case to win the room.
Names deaths, wounded, and depleted missile stocks as costs of the war, a critique built to win voters over to its side.
It states a shipping-flow consequence of the war, a material fact about the conflict's effects, in a line aimed at persuading.
It ties the war directly to rising oil, diesel and consumer prices, which is the object's core cost substance.
Says the war is still going on despite promises it would end, a claim about the war's duration aimed at winning the audience against the administration.
Forecasts no near-term relief at the pump, a cost claim about the object built to rally voters against the administration.
